stage: initial inspection before editor proposals or candidates
sourceObservations: The supplied snapshot shows a tall pale faceted pillar on a broad square foot. Stone crown is washed out, cool cyan-gray side shading is broad and flat, moss is represented by a few bright green block shapes, and the fracture is a thin dark stroke.

The directly opened immutable Blender library has a canonical identity root at ground (0,0,0), ten mesh parts, no armature and no declared sockets or port profiles. Actual physical source bounds are [-.5,-.5,0] to [.5,.5,1.7990000248]. Nominal catalog height 1.88 is distinct from that measured source maximum.
The generic repeated terrain interaction is not evidence of a connector contract; this standalone column needs footprint/contact/scale review rather than artificial seam matching.
targetObservations: The fixed ImageGen target makes pale stone read as warm ivory with softly rounded fractured volumes, a broken crown with distinct stone ledges, broad natural moss pads and growth following cracks. The base has a more crafted weathered stone construction. These are permitted useful design improvements.

The target uses clear large cracks, small stone chips and warm/cool surface variation. Fine mottling and the exact crack map are secondary to readable volume and crown/moss silhouette at the registered game scale.

The target is one artistic view with a different raw canvas from the source. Its apparent scale/camera/registration and directional brighter left side are not technical evidence or requirements; target edge contamination or halos must not be copied.
comparativePriorities: Replace the source blank washed-out pillar and cubic moss with readable warm stone volume and purposeful native broken-crown/moss forms.
Keep pale warm stone versus lime/olive moss separation and soft broad shading in all actual rotated views; preserve the pale-column role.
At logical 192x320/128px-cell scale retain silhouette, major cracks and moss masses without black recesses, bright clipped patches, jaggies, floating geometry or floor shadow.
